title: Iconizing of Literature, Art, Humanities, and Science : Intermediality and Value in Popular Culture
summary: People wear Shakespeare quotes or Žižek portraits because certain works, figures, or concepts have become cultural icons, while others remain overlooked. Such icons embody what is seen as outstanding in culture and are either venerated or challenged through acts of iconoclasm. This volume explores from an interdisciplinary perspective how cultural meaning is created, communicated, and enacted in everyday life.
